steps.title: A long ا, not a doubled letter
body: Form III's signature is a long ا inserted right after the first root consonant, giving the shape فَاعَلَ — not to be confused with Form II's doubled middle consonant, which lands one letter later and is written differently even though the two can sound similar in fast speech.
سَافَرَ ("to travel"), already in your vocabulary since A1, is a Form III verb: سَافَرَ, present tense يُسَافِرُ.

Form III most often shifts a Form I verb into something done toward, or together with, someone — a reciprocal sense, or effort directed at someone. Later in this unit, Form VI adds a تَ prefix to this very pattern to make that reciprocal sense explicit.

steps.title: Form III in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form III. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: سَافَرَ (to travel) has a long ا right after the first letter. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: فَاعَلَ inserts a long alif after the first root consonant — the mark of Form III, different from Form II's doubled middle consonant.

steps.title: Meaning tendency
steps.prompt: What does Form III most often add to a Form I verb's meaning?

options.label: A reciprocal sense, or effort directed toward someone
Seeking or considering something to be true

steps.explanation: Form III's long alif most often shifts the action toward or together with someone. The causative sense belongs to Forms II and IV; "seeking or considering" belongs to Form X — both elsewhere in this unit.

steps.title: Two forms down
steps.message: Form III — long ا after the first letter, often reciprocal or effort-toward-someone. On to Form IV.
